page: Microsoft Azure E112ibds_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized instance engineered for enterprise workloads requiring extensive RAM, dedicated compute capacity, and substantial local high-speed storage. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the server provides 112 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 56 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware capabilities include 48 MB of L3 cache, hardware cryptographic extensions including VAES and SHA-NI, and AVX-512 vector support with VNNI instructions. The instance supplies 672 GB of system memory, matching a 6 GB per core density, and includes 4,080 GB of integrated local SSD storage.

Benchmark evaluations reflect exceptional multi-threaded parallel throughput alongside capable memory subsystems. In multi-core assessments, the instance achieves high-ranking marks across stress-ng multi-core tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and Clang compilation runs. Cryptographic throughput ranks in the top tier due to specialized hardware instruction support. Memory throughput reaches 337.25 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB block reads and 135.59 GB/sec for block writes. In-memory and caching tests demonstrate 97.4 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database scores. Conversely, single-threaded metrics remain within average bands, and large language model text generation without dedicated GPU acceleration demonstrates strict processing bottlenecks.

With its combination of 112 dedicated vCPUs, 672 GB RAM, and 4,080 GB local SSD storage, the E112ibds_v5 delivers high resource density on a single tenant-isolated footprint. It is well-suited for large relational databases, in-memory data grids, high-concurrency caching tiers, massive software build pipelines, and transactional enterprise applications requiring strong isolation.
description: Microsoft Azure E112ibds_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 112 dedicated vCPUs across 56 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz. Based on x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 672 GB of system memory, providing 6 GB per core, and includes 4,080 GB of high-speed local SSD storage. Benchmark results show strong multi-threaded execution, high cryptographic throughput via AVX-512 and VAES, and robust memory bandwidth capable of 337.25 GB/sec uncached reads and 97.4 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking hardware accelerators, it displays constrained throughput on large parameter LLM generation. The instance delivers dedicated hardware isolation and dense memory scaling tailored for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data processing, and large-scale compilation workloads.
